summary: This is a deliberately broken version of the RobotPet class: its show_talent method now returns one fixed sentence instead of a talent built from the pet's own name and mood. Running the tests against it shows which tests catch the change.

lines.text: The constructor is untouched, so every test that only checks the stored attributes still passes; that is why just two of the four tests fail rather than all of them.
The mood is still stored on the object, but show_talent no longer looks at it. Data can sit on an object completely unused, and nothing about running the program tells you that happened.
This is the sabotage. Every pet now reports the same talent, and because there are no {} placeholders left, the f prefix does nothing at all here.

Printing a pet's talent still looks plausible on screen, so a human skim would not catch the bug. The assertions in the test file compare against the exact expected sentence, which is what makes the failure visible; restore the original return once you have seen it.
